body:
Fixes #134

I went through every log, annotation, actionlint/shellcheck finding and zizmor finding of the main runs on `4bfa252`. I also ran the repository's workflow policy tests against main. This pull request fixes every false negative, false positive and warning that came from this repository. Only checks that need a repository owner still fail on main, and each prints what to do. The case study is in
[`dev/log/issues/134/pulls/135/analysis/README.md`](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/blob/issue-134-3fbe4eecd082/dev/log/issues/134/pulls/135/analysis/README.md). It maps each requirement to a commit, its evidence and its regression test.

### False negatives

- **Rust releases were never committed.** crates.io received 1.0.6, 1.0.7 and 1.0.8, but `rust/Cargo.toml` on main stayed at 0.1.0 and all 47 changelog fragments stayed in place.
  - Root cause: `rust/CHANGELOG.md` did not exist, so staging failed silently and the script reported "No changes to commit" with exit 0. The workflow then published anyway.
  - The release now:
    - creates the changelog and consumes the fragments;
    - verifies the written files;
    - rebases first, and retries only lost push races;
    - tags after the push.
  - `dev/log/.../scripts/repro-rust-release-commit.sh` shows the behaviour before (exit 0, nothing pushed) and after (one commit and tag `rust-v1.0.9`).
- **C# release ordering and safety.**
  - It now rebases before bumping, classifies push failures (GH006/GH013 rule rejections fail at once) and tags after the push.
  - It no longer interpolates release text into a shell.
  - A missing `NUGET_API_KEY` used to print "skipping" and pass. It now fails. NuGet trusted publishing is supported through `NUGET_USER`, as in the csharp template.
- **C# code without a changeset only warned.** The check also had a shellcheck SC2193 comparison that could never match, and a template injection.
- **The workflow-level concurrency groups cancelled queued main runs.** Concurrency is now set per job, and writer jobs use never-cancelled groups.
- **Both file-size checks matched exclusions as substrings.** As a result, `.github/**`, `rust/src/sequences/target_matcher.rs` and `rust/examples/lino_binary_dump.rs` were never checked. Exclusions now match whole path components.
- **`cargo audit` passed with warning-level advisories.** It now runs with `--deny warnings`.
- **The dependency check missed pins.** It ignored SHA/digest pins, exact action tags, `cargo install --version` and `pipx run pkg==ver`. It now reads them, which found outdated `wasm-pack` and `crates-io-auth-action` pins; both are bumped.
- **Nothing linted the workflows.** The new `workflows.yml` runs:
  - actionlint with shellcheck;
  - zizmor, in regular mode and a high-severity pedantic pass;
  - the policy tests, on every `.github/**` change.
- **Unpinned `*-latest` runners changed OS silently.** They are pinned to `ubuntu-24.04`, `macos-26` and `windows-2025`.
- **Coverage never reached Codecov.** Tokenless uploads are rejected for this repository, and `fail_ci_if_error: false` hid the error. Uploads now use `CODECOV_TOKEN` and fail loudly.
- **A failed registry lookup counted as "not published".** The release decisions guessed instead of failing:
  - Rust `check-release-needed.rs` and `version-and-commit.rs` read any failed crates.io, Docker Hub or GitHub request as "not published". One dropped connection made main republish 1.0.8 and fail with a misleading "bug in version bumping". The new shared `rust/scripts/registry.rs` retries transport errors, 429 and 5xx, treats only 404 as "not found", and fails with `::error title=crates.io lookup failed::` once the attempts run out.
  - `js-client.yml` read every `npm view` failure as "not on npm yet". Only `code E404` means that now; any other failure stops the job.
  - `check-web-archive.mjs` reported "No archived version" for a rate-limited (429) Wayback lookup, which archive.org returned for this host. It now retries and reports a lookup that keeps failing as a failed lookup.
  - The dependency check and the C# release lookups ran every request once, so the Dependencies run on `0653ed0` failed on one dropped nuget.org connection. They now retry network errors, 429 and 5xx with backoff, and name the network cause.
- **The C# release dropped a changeset it could not parse.** A changeset with a typo in its bump type (`minr`) was skipped with a warning and then deleted. The release went green as a patch, and the change was missing from the changelog. Both release scripts now fail with `::error title=Invalid changeset::` and keep every file.
- **Security findings in the workflows.** zizmor reported 126 findings, 23 of them high. Third-party actions are now pinned, untrusted values pass through `env`, checkouts no longer persist credentials, and permissions are scoped per job.

### False positives and warnings

- **C# tests on macOS aborted at random** with `Unhandled exception. System.ArgumentNullException: Value cannot be null. (Parameter 'socket')` in `LinksServer.HandleConnection`. This hit run 40086095559 on this branch (no C# change) and run 38697246013 on main. It is a real race in the server: a worker called `TcpClient.GetStream()` while `Shutdown` disposed that client. `TcpClient` reads its socket after the `Connected` check, and the socket is `null` once disposed. The accept loop now takes the stream under the lock `Shutdown` holds. The strengthened test crashes the old code in 20 of 20 runs.

- **Green releases carried a red `No Trusted Publishing config found` annotation.** crates.io trusted publishing now runs only when the `CRATES_IO_TRUSTED_PUBLISHING` variable is `true`, and `continue-on-error` is banned.
- **Green C# and WebAssembly runs showed an `::error title=C# release failed::` annotation.** It leaked from an expected test failure. Test helpers now capture child stdio.
- **Codecov uploaded a Rust test file as a coverage report** and printed xcrun, gcov and coverage.py warnings. The upload is now restricted to the test results directory with `plugins: noop`.
- **Other warnings removed:**
  - the 903-line file-size warning, fixed by removing a duplicated function;
  - the CodeQL C# autobuild overlay warning and the template-copy analyzer warnings;
  - deploy-pages `DEP0040`;
  - wasm-pack's missing LICENSE warning;
  - the `init.defaultBranch` hint in every checkout;
  - the opaque `fetch failed` message, which now logs its cause.

### Needs a repository owner

On main each of these fails with an explicit message; pull requests stay green.

- **Codecov:** activate the repository on Codecov and add the `CODECOV_TOKEN` secret. Until then the `Codecov Token` job fails on main, but releases are not blocked.
- **npm:** add `NPM_TOKEN`. Once the package exists, you can configure `js-client.yml` as its trusted publisher instead. `Release to npm` already failed on main before this pull request.
- **Optional:**
  - crates.io trusted publishing plus the `CRATES_IO_TRUSTED_PUBLISHING=true` variable;
  - a nuget.org trusted publishing policy plus `NUGET_USER`.

  Without these, the existing token secrets keep publishing.

### Template reports

The same defects exist in the pipeline templates and are reported there, with reproductions, workarounds and suggested fixes:

- https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/issues/217: `check-file-size.rs` substring exclusions.
- https://github.com/link-foundation/csharp-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/issues/74: `check-file-size.mjs` substring exclusions.
- https://github.com/link-foundation/csharp-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/issues/75: the Codecov upload searches the whole checkout, and a missing token never fails.
- https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/issues/218: a failed crates.io, Docker Hub or GitHub lookup counts as "not published".
- https://github.com/link-foundation/csharp-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/issues/76: the NuGet and GitHub release lookups run once, so one dropped connection fails the release.
- https://github.com/link-foundation/csharp-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/issues/78: an unparseable changeset is skipped and then deleted, so its bump and description vanish.
- Wayback lookups that fail are reported as "No archived version" in all three templates: https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/issues/219, https://github.com/link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/issues/261 and https://github.com/link-foundation/csharp-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/issues/77.

The js template's line-limit check is not affected, its release lookups never guess "not published", and `changeset version` rejects an unparseable changeset there. The CodeQL autobuild warning is already tracked as csharp template issue #73.

### Validation

Each fix has a regression test that fails against the previous code:

- **Workflow policy and dependency-check tests:** 155 pass (`node --test .github/scripts/*.test.mjs`).
- **C# release and file-size script tests:** 39 pass (`node --test csharp/scripts/*.test.mjs`).
- **C# library tests:** 553 pass (`dotnet test`).
- **Rust script suites:** 29 tests in 4 suites (`bash rust/scripts/test-scripts.sh`).
- **Reproductions:** each fix that needed one has a script under `dev/log/issues/134/pulls/135/scripts` and its before/after output under `analysis`.
- **actionlint 1.7.12 and zizmor 1.31.1:** no findings.

**CI on `b6277ea`:** all 9 workflows pass (C#, Rust, JS client, WebAssembly, Docs, Workflows, Security, Dependencies, Broken Link Checker). The only annotations are notices: the intended `CODECOV_TOKEN` notice and GitHub's macOS runner capacity notice.
title: Fix false positives, false negatives, warnings and errors in CI/CD
